title: A Thousand Mountains | Aries
subtitle: For you and me, ten years ago
body:
Once upon a time I wished To keep you by my side The castle we built was too careless In just a moment, you were gone I recall your smile I remember your embrace So ardent I was about to melt Waking at midnight—in whose arms are you playing?
That ardent Aries Both kind and wild Hoofbeats clatter, clatter, clatter I am not that homeland[1] Tree shadows, the moon Even the mistletoe is melancholy
A moment of youthful madness Loving with sound and color, unabashed Flowers bloom upon the dust You are the ideal of this human world You are my heartbeat And also poison
You, one of a kind Me, dispensable How lucky I am to have met you Then to orbit you, to be your Charon, never to fail you[2]
How brave that Aries So brave, so hard to forget Why does the rose pierce The heart that loves her so deeply? Forget the sunset This planet has no ocean
A moment of youthful madness Loving with sound and color, unabashed Flowers bloom upon the dust We are both growing The river of stars can no longer burn hot The ideal has gone out
--- **Translator’s notes** [1] The hoofbeats and homeland recall Zheng Chouyu’s poem *Mistake*: the sound of approaching hooves is mistaken for a homecoming. [2] Charon is Pluto’s moon. “Orbit” retains the celestial image of 环游 here.
